text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Under the pressure of Ankara and the international community, Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash announces he will go to the second round of formal United Nations talks at Montreux, Switzerland.
- Turkish Prime Minister Mesut Yilmaz reiterates Ankara will not tolerate the deployment of a Russian surface to air missile system on Cyprus.
- Denktash is to attend the Switzerland talks.
- Four British soldiers are charged with assault after an attack on two British tourists in Ayia Napa.

- Pavlos Georgiou, the Cypriot who was jailed for 15 months for negligently infecting British lover Janette Pink with the HIV virus which causes AIDS, denies allegations in a British tabloid that he slept with "more than 1,000 women".
- Communist Akel calls for an inquiry in Cyprus to find the associates of the Greek junta which was responsible for overthrowing the late president, Archbishop Makarios, in 1974.
- Rauf Denktash makes a U-turn and announces he will go to the next round of U.N.-sponsored talks.
- Mussels stuck in the plumbing system of a Cypriot-owned cruiseboat at Pireaus delayed its virgin voyage to Cyprus.
- Officials underline the need for legislation to put order to mismanagement noted by several cooperative credit societies. Punitive action should also be taken, says Commerce and Industry Minister.
